page: Vultr vx1-g-4c-16g-240s is a general-purpose virtual server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor with 4 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 2 physical cores and 2 threads per core, operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 240 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU metrics, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all ranking in the top tier. However, multi-threaded scaling presents a notable tradeoff; both the Geekbench multi-core score and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression fall into the bottom 25% tier. Memory bandwidth is average, reaching 440.06 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 70.96 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Database operations, Redis SET performance at 8.1 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput of 14.81 GB/sec all align with average tier expectations.

Given its dedicated AMD EPYC cores and NVMe storage, this server offers a balanced resource density suitable for workloads that require predictable single-core performance without the premium of high-end compute-optimized instances. It is recommended for general-purpose applications, text processing, software compilation, and moderate database operations. It is less optimal for highly parallelized multi-threaded tasks or large-scale language model inference, where its multi-core and prompt processing speeds are constrained.
